subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: Slewfoot: A Tale of Bewitchery
novels.author: Brom (2021)
novels.vibe: A lush, illustrated Puritan-era horror novel about a widow accused of witchcraft who forms a bargain with an ancient forest spirit.
novels.summary: In 1666 colonial Connecticut, newly widowed Abitha is targeted by her suspicious, hostile community right as a strange, ancient being awakens in the nearby woods and offers her his power. As Abitha embraces witchcraft to survive, the story builds toward a bloody reckoning between the Puritan settlement and the older, wilder forces it displaced.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence, sexual assault, religious persecution, animal death, torture, colonial-era brutality.

novels.title: Maggie's Grave
novels.author: David Sodergren (2021)
novels.vibe: A gleefully savage splatter-horror novel about a wronged 'witch' resurrected for bloody revenge on the village that killed her.
novels.summary: Centuries after being murdered by a Scottish village as a witch, Maggie Wall's grave is disturbed, resurrecting her and her fury at the descendants of those responsible. The novel turns into an over-the-top, deliriously violent revenge rampage through the modern-day town.
novels.warnings: Extreme graphic violence and gore, sexual assault, torture, animal death, dismemberment.

novels.title: The Year of the Witching
novels.author: Alexis Henderson (2020)
novels.vibe: A dark, feminist gothic about a rigid theocratic settlement, the witches haunting its cursed woods, and a girl who starts asking why.
novels.summary: In the strict, patriarchal settlement of Bethel, Immanuelle stumbles into the cursed forest bordering town and discovers her dead mother's journal, hinting at forbidden secrets. As she's drawn deeper into the witches' power and the truth behind Bethel's founding, she becomes a threat to the church that rules it.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence, religious abuse and extremism, sexual assault, self-harm, body horror, misogyny.

novels.title: Red Rabbit
novels.author: Alex Grecian (2022)
novels.vibe: A blood-soaked Weird Western about a witch-hunting party crossing a Kansas plagued by supernatural horrors.
novels.summary: A witch and a gunslinger reluctantly team up with a ragtag group crossing the post-Civil War Kansas plains, hunting a powerful and monstrous witch responsible for a string of horrors. Along the way the group encounters a string of supernatural threats that turn the journey into a violent, episodic nightmare.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and gore, body horror, animal death, racism (period-typical), sexual content.

short_works.title: The White People
short_works.author: Arthur Machen (1904)
short_works.vibe: A hallucinatory, dreamlike weird-fiction classic told through a young girl's increasingly disturbing secret diary of witchcraft and hidden rites.
short_works.summary: Framed by a philosophical discussion of true evil, the story presents the diary of a young girl who is gradually initiated into a secret, ancient tradition of witchcraft and folklore by her nurse. The diary's dreamlike, fragmented prose builds an atmosphere of creeping wrongness rather than explicit horror.
short_works.warnings: Disturbing/ambiguous themes of ritual abuse, child endangerment, unsettling occult imagery.

short_works.title: This Town Doesn't Exist on Any Map
short_works.author: Tobias Wade (2019)
short_works.vibe: A viral creepypasta-style story about a driver who stumbles into an impossible small town that shouldn't exist — and can't seem to leave.
short_works.summary: A late-night wrong turn leads the narrator into a strange small town with no cell signal, no visible way out, and an escalating sense that something is deeply, deliberately wrong with its residents. As the narrator tries to find a way back to the highway, the town's true, witchcraft-tinged nature closes in.
short_works.warnings: Psychological horror, disturbing imagery, implied violence, isolation/entrapment themes.

short_works.title: Dreams in the Witch House
short_works.author: H.P. Lovecraft (1933)
short_works.vibe: A cosmic-horror take on witchcraft — a student's rented room in a crooked old house opens onto other dimensions, and a witch who never really left.
short_works.summary: A mathematics student rents a room in a notoriously crooked old Arkham house once inhabited by an executed witch, drawn by the building's strange non-Euclidean geometry. His studies of the room's angles begin to open dream-visions of other realities, and of the witch and her monstrous familiar, still very much active.
short_works.warnings: Child sacrifice, graphic violence, body horror, disturbing occult imagery, period-typical racism.

short_works.title: Viy
short_works.author: Nikolai Gogol (1835)
short_works.vibe: A Ukrainian folk-horror classic about a seminary student trapped reciting prayers over the corpse of a witch for three increasingly terrifying nights.
short_works.summary: After a fatal encounter with an old woman who turns out to be a witch, seminarian Khoma Brutus is ordered to keep vigil over her body in a remote church for three nights. Each night grows more nightmarish as the witch's corpse and the demonic forces she commands close in around him.
short_works.warnings: Death, supernatural/demonic threat, disturbing imagery, religious horror.
